survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, student-level analytic sample, or survey-weight variables. The tables describe governance structures and expenditure shares across federal, regional (Länder), and local (municipal) levels, not survey-based measurement of student achievement. As a result, there are no plausible values (PV) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) to apply. For any future quantitative work using ILSA microdata, analysts would need to use the official ILSA sampling weights and replicate weights provided by the data producer; this note itself provides none.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a governance country note describing institutional responsibilities and expenditure shares in Germany’s adult skills system; it does not model cognitive achievement outcomes from ILSA-style test scores. Because there is no PV-based dependent variable and no student-level assessment dataset analyzed, plausible values are not applicable. Missing-data handling is not reported because no statistical estimation on microdata is conducted in this note.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA microdata are used. The note compiles governance and expenditure information for Germany and reports governance/expenditure shares by level of government (federal, Länder, local) without defining an analytic student sample.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Germany country note summarizes how the adult skills system is governed across federal, regional (Länder), and local (municipal) levels, and how responsibilities are allocated across policy areas (VET, HVET, CET, adult education/AE, and ALMPs). It reports expenditure shares at the subnational level (48.9% total, with 31.5% to state level and 17.4% to local level) and provides structured tables mapping which governance level is responsible for strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, and delivery. The note describes a combined governance structure: national authorities retain overarching strategic and funding responsibility, while states and municipalities implement key components. It also details stakeholder roles (ministries, federal institutes, the Federal Employment Agency, PES regional directorates, vocational training committees, competent bodies/chambers, and adult education centres). No ILSA assessment design, sampling, scaling, or PV-based benchmarking is performed; therefore, there are no model performance metrics or achievement benchmarks to interpret.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical large-scale assessment analysis and contains no student-level dataset, sampling design, or statistical modeling. Consequently, fields required for ML/PV-based empirical studies (e.g., plausible values handling, missing-data strategy, sample sizes, and main findings with predictive metrics) are intentionally absent because the document is descriptive and policy-institutional in nature.
